description:
Hi! I'm Anaswara KS from Kerala, India. I'm a Machine Learning student passionate about AI, data science, and solving real-world problems using technology. I'm participating in this hackathon with my project EnvKo Trend, which focuses on analysing environmental and climate changes in Kochi using NASA Earth observation data and exploring future climate trends.
I'm looking for passionate teammates interested in climate science ,web development,ML,UI/UX design. Let's collaborate and build together!
summary:
EnvKo Trend is an interactive climate analysis and forecasting web application developed as a solution to the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!”

The project uses historical climate data from NASA POWER for Kochi, Kerala, covering January 2001 to October 2026. It analyzes five climate parameters: average, maximum and minimum temperature, monthly rainfall, and average humidity.

EnvKo Trend helps users explore historical climate patterns, identify long-term trends, and detect unusual variations through interactive graphs and visualizations. It also uses statistical models (SARIMA) to generate monthly temperature, rainfall, and humidity forecasts for 2027.

The application is developed using Python, Pandas, NumPy, Plotly, and Streamlit. Statistical analysis includes the Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope, and STL decomposition. ChatGPT and Google Gemini were used as debugging assistance during development.

The main goal is to transform complex NASA climate data into simple, understandable insights and help people explore how the local climate is changing over time.
details:
Project Details – EnvKo Trend

EnvKo Trend is an interactive climate analysis and forecasting web application developed as a solution to the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!” The project focuses on Kochi, Kerala, and aims to make climate data easier for people to explore and understand.

What does it do and how does it work?

The application uses historical climate data from NASA POWER, covering January 2001 to October 2026. It analyzes five climate parameters: average temperature, maximum temperature, minimum temperature, monthly rainfall, and average humidity.

The data is collected through the NASA POWER API, cleaned, and converted from daily observations into monthly records. The application then:

  • Displays historical climate patterns through interactive graphs.
  • Identifies long-term climate trends.
  • Highlights unusual monthly variations using STL decomposition.
  • Generates monthly temperature, rainfall, and humidity forecasts for 2027 using SARIMA models.

What are its benefits?

  • Makes complex climate data easier to understand.
  • Helps users explore historical climate changes in Kochi.
  • Highlights unusual climate variations.
  • Provides a simple way to visualize possible future climate patterns.

What is the intended impact?

The main goal is to improve awareness and understanding of local climate patterns by transforming NASA's climate data into meaningful visual insights. It encourages people to explore environmental changes using real data.

What tools and technologies were used?

  • Programming language: Python
  • Data processing: Pandas, NumPy
  • Visualization: Plotly
  • Web application: Streamlit
  • Statistical analysis: Mann-Kendall Test, Sen's Slope, STL Decomposition
  • Forecasting: SARIMA
  • Development tools: VS Code, Jupyter Notebook
  • Version control: Git and GitHub
  • AI-assisted debugging: ChatGPT and Google Gemini

How is the project creative?

EnvKo Trend combines historical climate exploration, trend identification, unusual variation detection, and statistical forecasting in one interactive dashboard. Instead of presenting climate information as complicated tables, it converts the data into visual insights that are easier to explore.

What factors were considered?

The project considered data availability, historical coverage, location relevance, data quality, visualization clarity, forecasting accuracy, and the limitations of statistical predictions. NASA POWER provides gridded estimates rather than direct measurements at every local location, and the forecasts are statistical estimates, not exact weather predictions.

Overall, EnvKo Trend connects NASA's Earth data with local climate understanding, helping users explore what has changed, identify unusual patterns, and investigate what might happen next.
